AI is accelerating to rewrite the processes and paperwork of production managers, but on-site judgment and professional experience still need to be carried out by humans - this article breaks down the specific impacts and response paths.

Not suitable for people who are afraid of taking responsibility, can't sit still, and are insensitive to numbers. Dispatch and emergency are often linked, and carelessness can lead to downtime or even accidents.
The common path is: operation/maintenance technology → duty leader → production supervisor → hydropower production manager → plant-level or regional management.

Suitable for people who are stable, understand the system, and can handle the pressure of scheduling. If you are willing to take "safe and stable development" as the standard, then this business will be stable.

The hydropower production manager coordinates the power generation process and unit operation and maintenance of the hydropower station, and is responsible for load dispatch, maintenance coordination, safety compliance and team management.

paragraphs: The morning meeting determines the load and maintenance for the day; the day shift monitors the water level and unit curve, and receives dispatching instructions to adjust the load; the rainy season monitors the flood forecast and arranges storage capacity; the midday inspection and maintenance progress; emergency load reduction immediately when the machine is out of service; and checks the daily report and schedules tomorrow's window before get off work.

In a word: Make the power station safe and stable. Specifically, load adjustment, arranging maintenance, monitoring water levels, team management, ensuring safety, and connecting to the power grid. It uses both brains and responsibility, and is the center of production operations.

According to data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), there will be approximately 241,900 production managers on the job in 2024, and this number is expected to rise to 246,500 by 2034, with a net increase of approximately 4,600 positions, an average of approximately 17,100 job vacancies per year, and a median annual salary of approximately US$121,400 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI won’t replace hydropower production managers, but it will compress monitoring. Predictive maintenance and intelligent dispatch speed up routine load adjustment, and managers move from "monitoring the curve" to "safety decision-making, dispatch coordination, emergency command, team and compliance management." Those who are really squeezed out are those who only monitor screens. People who understand hydraulic engineering and electrical engineering are more valuable.
